THE PERSIANS
934-1629 CE
IRANIAN DYNASTIES, DIVANS, TRADE
Difficulty: 3 stars

The collapse of the Sassanian Empire saw Persia fall into disunity for over 700 years. Yet, in spite of its fractionalization, Persian culture, language, and martial traditions continued to foster and grow. In Age of Empires IV, the Persian civilization represents the various medieval dynasties, both native and foreign, that ruled over the region of “Ērān.” In-game, Persia sports a powerful economy, with an emphasis on trade and flexibility. In combat, this is THE “counter” civ, with units that are weaker at a base level, but much more effective against their counters.

STRENGTHS:
Strong economy enabled by Divans that can supervise.
Flexible - can easily switch army compositions.
Very strong trade!
Zamburak Siege Camels!

WEAKNESSES:
Cannot upgrade unit Veterancy seperately.
Units are weak in general-purpose roles.
Weak in early Imperial due to expensive techs.

UNIQUE UNITS:
Qizilbash: Fast moving Horse Archer that deals bonus damage to melee units.
Daylamite: Cheap Man-at-arms with less armor, but deals bonus damage to light infantry.
Savar: Slow, tanky Lancer with an anti-armor mace attack.
Assassin*: Stealthed killer that first strikes for double damage. Can’t attack buildings but can Sabotage them.
Zamburak*: Siege Camelry. Functions like Mounted Ozutsu. Place it in the Archery Range just like the Grenadier.

IRANIAN DYNASTIES:
Medieval Iran was a melting pot of diverse cultures and transient empires. Each conquering dynasty brought their own veteran forces with them. This is represented in-game by the Dynasty system.

Unlike other civilization’s units, Persian units do not research veterancy individually. Instead, all of your units are upgraded simultaneously as you upgrade your dynasty.

Buyid (Regular) ➟ Khwarazmid (Hardened) ➟ Il-Khanid (Veteran) ➟ Safavid (Elite)

MILITARY SPECIALIZATION:
All of Persia’s unique units have less base damage but more bonus damage vs. the units they counter. This makes them weaker as generalist units but much stronger as specialist units.

INFLUENCE - DYNASTIC BUREAUCRACY:
Each time you advance your Dynasty, you can build an additional Divan. Divans are special buildings that can supervise nearby structures (think Chinese Imperial Official, but in the form of a building). Choose either:

Divan of Commerce:
Houses unique economic technologies. Emits an aura range of 4 units.
Ability: Commerce Vizier - Supervise a nearby economic drop-off, granting +20% bonus resources and improving research speed (does not affect Town Centers, Docks, or Markets).

Divan of War:
Houses unique military technologies. Emits an influence range of 4 units.
Ability: War Vizier - Supervise a military production or technology building within the Divan’s influence, boosting its military production or research speed by +150%.

UNIQUE BUILDING: CARAVANSERAI:
Unique structure that massively buffs nearby Traders’ movement speed and armor. Unlocked in the Castle Age.

TURKOMAN HORSE ARCHERS:
In the Feudal Age unlock the Qizilbash, a unique Horse Archer that counters melee units. In Age IV, research Turkoman Traditions to enable the Qizilbash to attack while moving, just like Mongol Mangudai.

GARDEN BOUNTY:
Mills constructed near Berry Bushes create Orchards, increasing Food capacity by +100. Gather from Berry Bushes +30% faster, but cannot gather from Boar. Berry carry capacity increased +3.

Minor:
We cannot affect unit visuals, building visuals, voice lines, sound effects, music, or image assets, so all assets are recycled.

Medieval Iran was a melting pot of diverse cultures and transient empires. Each conquering dynasty brought their own veteran forces with them. This is represented in-game by the Dynasty system.

Unlike other civilization’s units, Persian units do not research veterancy individually. Instead, all of your units are upgraded simultaneously as you upgrade your dynasty.

Buyid (Regular) ➟ Khwarazmid (Hardened) ➟ Il-Khanid (Veteran) ➟ Safavid (Elite)
